evidence_reviewed: ES query covering the injection window
Health witness log: only audit DOWN then RECOVERED -- no other service flagged, unlike the multi-service MongoDB case

audit own logs: HEALTH_CHECK_FAILED at 11:20:06.6, then a direct ConnectionInitException referencing 127.0.0.1:9042 (Cassandra own port), plus Kafka consumer-group offset-seeking/retry activity and Error handler exceptions

Funnel counts across the rest of the pipeline (gateway/validation/aml/routing/settlement) are essentially normal (14 submitted, 11 validated, 11 routed, 11 settled) -- no stall anywhere but audit, consistent with audit consuming asynchronously via Kafka rather than blocking the payment path
reasoning_trace: First live test of CASSANDRA_OUTAGE. Witness independently flagged only audit DOWN then RECOVERED. audit own log stream shows a direct connection error to 127.0.0.1:9042, Cassandra own port, plus visible Kafka consumer retry/offset-seeking behavior consistent with a downstream sink falling behind while its backing store is unavailable. No other service showed any degradation, and the payment funnel proceeded normally end to end -- audit logging is evidently async (Kafka-consumed) rather than a blocking dependency for the main payment path. Conclusion reached from evidence alone, before reading the injectors own log: cassandra.
confirmation_basis: Blind conclusion (cassandra) matches the injectors own ground-truth log exactly. Clean single-dependency case: unlike MONGODB_OUTAGE (which surprised us with a second dependent service), CASSANDRA_OUTAGE behaved exactly as the code-level dependency mapping predicted -- only audit affected, direct port-9042 evidence, no funnel-wide stall since audit is async. Cassandra recovered cleanly within its extended 90s window despite documented OOM/slow-restart history -- no infra problem this run.
